bug_semantics: XORMappedAddress.GetFromAs decodes the STUN address family with bin.Uint16(value[0:2]) before checking that the XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS attribute value is long enough. Message.Decode stores attr.Value as a subslice of the remaining buffer (b[:aL]); STUN pads lengths 1–3 to 4 bytes, but a 0-length value has no padding. When that 0-length attribute is last in a tightly allocated Raw buffer (cap==len), the value slice has cap 0, so value[0:2] is a runtime slice-bounds panic. A remote Binding-success (or any parsed STUN/ICE message) carrying a trailing 0-length XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS therefore DoSes the process (CWE-20). The later len(value)<=4 check sat after the family read and could not prevent this panic.
flaw_origin: The surviving panic is the conjunction of (1) XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS family decode from v[0:2] without a prior length>=2 check and (2) attribute lookup that returns a present but empty value. (1) was first written in bf2972d5019e2cb37713b244e5666a768bfb07dc (GetXORMappedAddress) behind if len(v)==0 { return ErrAttributeNotFound }, which treated a 0-length present attribute as missing and blocked this PoC. (2) was introduced by 2d0e6be7ebff885c354ee08b968f7cbcd72cf9b6: Attributes.Get switched from returning BlankAttribute to (attr, ok), and getAttrValue switched from len(v)==0 to !ok, so a present 0-length value reached binary.BigEndian.Uint16(v[0:2]). That lookup semantics was copied into Message.Get (fba9f6b02da38b64c47b5a9fd60d77c5ac44527b) and GetFrom/GetFromAs (0c49de1e6f2efd9b1cee594c251c2506a51c9b32, a rename/extract, not a first-write). 1b68c7e31a6fd27b848a7101edea22f31b800128 added the len<=4 check after the family read (incomplete crasher fix). Pre-gortc pion v0.2.2 XorAddress.Unpack checked len(v) before the family read and was not this bug; 779613246e6143d325ebac08b2bd38d32a6d651b imported the already-vulnerable gortc code as pion v0.3 and is a merge, not a BIC.

The attack is a well-formed STUN header plus a trailing 0-length XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS on a no-spare-capacity buffer; Decode yields a 0-cap value, GetFromAs slices [0:2] before the length check, and the process panics. git log -L on GetFromAs plus -S on the lookup helper shows the family-read line predates GetFromAs: GetFromAs is a 2017 rename of GetFrom, which is a refactor of GetXORMappedAddress. Later commits (Message.Get, GetFromAs extract, late len<=4 check, golangci renames, gortc→pion merge) move or incompletely patch the same mechanism and are not BICs.
